header: Mr.Zafar Ali Shah Rizvi for the petitioner.
body: DR. RANA MUHAMMAD SHAMIM, J. The petitioner assailed the impugned judgment dated 16.4.2007 in Suit No.12/2007 passed by Senior Civil Judge/Family Judge, Moro, whereby the respondent No.1 was granted ‘khula’ by dissolving marriage between her and the petitioner whereas other prayers were not allowed.

2. Briefly the respondent No.1 had filed suit for dissolution of marriage stating therein that she entered into marriage ties with the petitioner according to Sharia in the month of January 2006. No Nikahnama was reduced in writing nor marriage was registered due to illiteracy and unawareness of the parties. At the time of marriage prompt dower was fixed as pair of golden Leelam but the same has not yet been paid by the petitioner to her despite her several demands. She stated in her suit that her parents gave dowry articles worth Rs.40,000/- which were taken by the petitioner, kept the same in his house at the time of her ‘rukhsati’. Such dowry articles are still lying at the house of the petitioner. Initially both petitioner and respondent No.1 lived together as husband and wife within the prescribed limits of Almighty Allah. Subsequently, differences arose between petitioner and the respondent No.1 as the behaviour of the petitioner subsequently changed and started quarelling on petty matters. At times she was insulted and maltreated which causes for strained relations between the couple. The petitioner found absolutely jobless having no means to maintain respondent No.1 properly. The petitioner allegedly was also indulged in immoral activities like intoxication, drinking liquor and gambling. At time she was physically beaten by the petitioner. Consequently petitioner drove her in three clothes. However, on the intervention of nekmards and well wishers, the petitioner and respondent No.1 again joined and started living together as husband and wife which could not prolong much. Subsequently she was again driven out from the house, which consequently created severe hatred feelings in the heart of respondent No.1 for petitioner. The respondent No.1 was constrained to decide not to stay with the petitioner as his wife. Due to such hatred feelings she was firm on her such decision. As a last resort, she approached to the learned Family Court and her suit was admitted on 22.1.2006. Upon hearing the marriage was dissolved between the petitioner and respondent No.1 and the ‘khula’ was granted to her in the circumstances.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner upon receiving notice had filed written statement in which he raised objection about the jurisdiction of the learned Family court is ousted on the ground that respondent No.1 was not permanently residing within the jurisdiction of learned trial court. He further submits that although the ‘khula’ was granted to respondent No.1 yet the learned trial court has not passed any order for the return of the monetary benefits achieved by the respondent No.1 during her stay with the petitioner. The judgment passed by the learned trial court is corum non judice. The impugned judgment and decree is illegal and without jurisdiction hence not tenable in law.

4. I have heard learned counsel for the petitioner and gone through the material available in case file. From the record it appears that at the time of filing family suit in the learned trial court she was ordinarily residing at Sindh Colony, U.C Fatoo Balal, Police Station, Moro, taluka Moro, district Naushahro Feroze which falls within the jurisdiction of the learned trial court. According to first proviso of Rule 6 of The Family Courts Rules, 1965 if the lady seeking ‘khula’ at the time of filing suit is ordinarily residing within the local limits of such Police Station which falls within the jurisdiction of the Family Court, the Family Court may take cognizance and decide the matter according to law. Rule 6 of The Family Courts Rules, 1965 is reproduced hereunder:
6. The Court which shall have jurisdiction to try a suit will be that within the local limits of which:--
(a) the cause of action wholly or in part has arisen; or
Provided that in suits for dissolution
of marriage or dower, the Court within the local limits of which the wife ordinarily resides shall also have jurisdiction.

5. In view of the above discussion, the respondent No.1 at the time of filing of suit was ordinarily residing within the local limits of Police Station, which falls within the jurisdiction of learned Family Court. The judgment and decree passed by the learned Family Court is legal and within its jurisdiction. No illegality or material irregularly has been pointed out in the impugned judgment. Further in my considered view if the wife states that she hates her husband and has decided not to live with him and firms on her such decision, the law does not require from the wife to explain such hatred feelings for her husband. If she is not ready to join her husband, she cannot be forced to live with him. Such forced union of husband and wife is not permissible in law. The impugned judgment is proper, legal and no interference is called for. The impugned judgment passed by the learned trial court is upheld. The petition was dismissed in limine by my short order dated 19.3.2008, above are the reasons for the said short order.
